title: Heat exhaustion or heatstroke
summary: Move to a cool place and cool immediately; altered mental status in heat is heatstroke.
sources: 2024 American Heart Association and American Red Cross Guidelines for First Aid — Hyperthermia and Heatstroke
2025 International Consensus on First Aid Science With Treatment Recommendations (ILCOR CoSTR) — First Aid Cooling Techniques
actions: Move the person out of heat, remove excess clothing, and begin cooling.

For suspected heatstroke, call emergency services and use cold-water immersion of the torso when practical. Otherwise use any immediately available active cooling: continuous wetting, fanning, cool shower, or ice packs to the neck, armpits, and groin.
Do not delay cooling while waiting for transport. Monitor breathing and stop cooling if severe shivering develops or when directed.
For milder heat exhaustion in a fully alert person who can swallow, rest in a cool place and give frequent sips of a carbohydrate-electrolyte drink or water.
If symptoms worsen, vomiting prevents drinking, or recovery is not rapid, obtain urgent medical care.
prohibitions: Do not give fluids to a confused, drowsy, seizing, or vomiting person.
Do not use fever medicine for heatstroke.
Do not delay emergency activation or cooling to measure an exact temperature.

redFlags.text: Emergency warning signs selected—contact emergency services now.

emergencyCall.text: Confusion, collapse, seizure, or reduced alertness in a hot person is heatstroke: call emergency services and cool immediately.
